questions.question: On the clock above the classroom door, the short hand is between the 3 and the 4, and the long hand points straight at the 7. What time is it?
questions.explain: The short hand gives the hour that it has already passed (3), and the long hand at the 7 means 7 groups of 5 minutes, so 7 × 5 = 35 minutes: 3:35. The usual trap is reading the long hand as the number 7 itself (3:07) or jumping the hour up to 4 before the clock actually reaches it.

questions.question: Maya's swimming lesson at the community pool starts at quarter past 8 in the morning. Which clock time is that?
questions.explain: A quarter of an hour is one of four equal parts of 60 minutes, so 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes, and ‘quarter past 8’ means 15 minutes after 8 o'clock: 8:15. Watch the words — ‘quarter past’ is after the hour, while ‘quarter to’ (7:45 or 8:45) is before the next hour, and ‘half past’ would be 8:30.

questions.question: On Noah's watch the short hand is just past the 2, and the long hand is 3 small marks past the 4. What time is it to the nearest minute?
questions.explain: Count by 5s to the 4 to get 20 minutes, then count on 3 single marks: 20 + 3 = 23 minutes, so the time is 2:23. Common traps are stopping at the 4 and saying 2:20, or adding the numbers 4 and 3 to get 2:07.

questions.question: The BC Ferries departure board shows Ravi's sailing leaving at 17:20. How would Ravi say this time using a.m. or p.m.?
questions.explain: Any 24-hour time from 13:00 onward is in the afternoon or evening, so subtract 12 from the hour and label it p.m.: 17 − 12 = 5, giving 5:20 p.m. The most common mistakes are subtracting 10 instead of 12 (7:20 p.m.) and keeping the 24-hour number while adding p.m., which says the same time twice.

questions.question: Jayden's soccer practice starts at 4:45 p.m. and lasts 50 minutes. What time does practice finish?
questions.explain: Count 15 minutes up to 5:00 p.m., then count on the 35 minutes that are left: 15 + 35 = 50, so practice ends at 5:35 p.m. The trap is adding 45 + 50 = 95 and writing 4:95 — once you pass 60 minutes you must regroup into a new hour — or forgetting that 15 of the 50 minutes were already used and landing on 5:50.

questions.question: Story time at the library begins at quarter to 11 and lasts half an hour. What time does it end?
questions.explain: Quarter to 11 is 10:45, and half an hour is 30 minutes, so 10:45 + 15 gets you to 11:00 and 15 more minutes makes 11:15. Two traps hide here: reading ‘quarter to 11’ as 11:15 instead of 10:45, and treating half an hour as 15 minutes instead of 30.

questions.question: The airport board shows Sofia's flight to Kelowna departing at 18:05. Her family wants to arrive at the airport 90 minutes before departure. What time should they arrive, said with a.m. or p.m.?
questions.explain: First change 18:05 to 12-hour time (18 − 12 = 6, so 6:05 p.m.), then count back 90 minutes as 1 hour and 30 minutes: back 1 hour is 5:05 p.m., back 30 more minutes is 4:35 p.m. The traps are subtracting 10 instead of 12 from the hour, counting back only the 1 hour and forgetting the 30 minutes, and switching to a.m. when the time is still in the afternoon.

questions.question: Liam's school bus leaves at 9:05 a.m. He checks the hall clock: the long hand is 2 small marks past the 11, and the short hand is very close to the 9 but has not reached it yet. How many minutes does Liam have until the bus leaves?
questions.explain: The short hand has not reached the 9 yet, so the hour is still 8, and the long hand shows 55 + 2 = 57 minutes, making it 8:57; from 8:57 it is 3 minutes to 9:00 plus 5 more minutes, so 8 minutes in all. The biggest trap is calling it 9:57 because the short hand looks like it is on the 9 — it only counts once it passes — and another is subtracting 57 from 105 as if an hour had 100 minutes.
